questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes You must answer on the multiple choice answer sheet. You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS  There are forty questions on this paper. Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 40.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper. A computer memory stick is labelled as having a storage capacity of 128GB. The letter B stands for byte, which is a unit. What is the equivalent storage capacity?

A man of mass 75.2kg uses a set of weighing scales to measure his mass three times. He obtains the following readings. mass/kg reading 1 80.2 reading 2 80.1 reading 3 80.2 Which statement describes the precision and accuracy of the weighing scales?

options.A: not precise to  0.1kg and accurate to  0.1kg
options.B: not precise to  0.1kg and not accurate to  0.1kg
options.C: precise to  0.1kg and accurate to  0.1kg
options.D: precise to  0.1kg and not accurate to  0.1kg

questions.questionText: Which statement about scalar and vector quantities is correct?

options.A: A scalar quantity has direction but not magnitude.
options.B: A scalar quantity has magnitude but not direction.
options.C: A vector quantity has direction but not magnitude.
options.D: A vector quantity has magnitude but not direction.

questions.questionText: How can the acceleration of an object be determined?

options.A: from the area under a displacement–time graph
options.B: from the area under a velocity–time graph
options.C: from the gradient of a displacement–time graph
options.D: from the gradient of a velocity–time graph

questions.questionText: A sprinter takes a time of 11.0s to run a 100m race. She first accelerates uniformly from rest, reaching a speed of 10ms–1. She then runs at a constant speed of 10ms–1 until the finish line. What is the uniform acceleration of the sprinter for the first part of the race?

A single horizontal force F is applied to a block X which is in contact with a separate block Y, as shown. F X Y The blocks remain in contact as they accelerate along a horizontal frictionless surface. Air resistance is negligible. X has a greater mass than Y. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The acceleration of X is equal to force F divided by the mass of X.
options.B: The force that X exerts on Y is equal to F.
options.C: The force that X exerts on Y is less than F.
options.D: The force that X exerts on Y is less than the force that Y exerts on X.

questions.questionText: A car of mass 750kg has a horizontal driving force of 2.0kN acting on it. It has a forward horizontal acceleration of 2.0ms–2. resistive force driving force What is the resistive force acting horizontally?

An object falls freely from rest in a vacuum. The graph shows the variation with time t of the velocity v of the object. v 0 t Which graph, using the same scales, represents the object falling in air?

options.A: B C D v v v v 0 0 0 0 0 t 0 t 0 t 0 t

questions.questionText: A rock of mass 2m, travelling in deep space at velocity v, explodes into two parts of equal mass, one of which is then stationary. What is the kinetic energy of the moving part after the explosion?

A horizontal metal bar PQ of length 50.0cm is hinged at end P. The diagram shows the metal bar viewed from above. 16.0 N 30° Q 5.0 N P 50.0 cm Two forces of 16.0N and 5.0N are in the horizontal plane and act on end Q, as shown. What is the resultant moment about P due to the two forces?

A cube WXZY has sides of length 2.0cm and mass 24.0g. The cube rests on a metre rule of negligible mass. The geometrical centre of the cube is vertically above the 70.0cm mark on the scale of the rule. mass 24.0 g mass W X NOT TO 23.4 g SCALE Y Z

50 69 71 The cube has a non-uniform density so that its centre of gravity is not at its geometrical centre. The centre of gravity of the cube is in the plane of the diagram. The rule rests on a pivot at the 50.0cm mark. A mass of 23.4g is placed vertically above the 30.0cm mark. The rule is horizontal and in equilibrium. What can be determined about the position of the centre of gravity of the cube?

options.A: It must be somewhere along a horizontal line that is 0.5cm from line WX.
options.B: It must be somewhere along a horizontal line that is 0.5cm from line YZ.
options.C: It must be somewhere along a vertical line that is 0.5cm from line WY.
options.D: It must be somewhere along a vertical line that is 0.5cm from line XZ.

questions.questionText: A rigid sphere is held at rest on the sea bed. When the sphere is released, it rises to the surface of the sea. The seawater has a uniform density. Which statement about the sphere, from its release until it reaches the surface, is correct?

options.A: The sphere always moves with constant acceleration.
options.B: The sphere always moves with constant velocity.
options.C: The upthrust on the sphere always decreases.
options.D: The upthrust on the sphere is always constant.

questions.questionText: What is a unit for density?

options.A: Nm–3 B gmm–1 C kgcm–2 D gmm–3

questions.questionText: The total energy input E in a process is partly transferred to useful energy output U and partly in transferred to energy that is wasted W. What is the efficiency of the process? U

options.B:  100% E in U

questions.questionText: An escalator is 60m long and lifts passengers through a vertical height of 30m, as shown.

A rock of mass 40kg is released from rest from a height of 20m above the surface of a planet. The rock has a kinetic energy of 32kJ when it hits the surface of the planet. The planet does not have an atmosphere. What is the weight of the rock on the surface of the planet?
A metal wire is stretched. The wire obeys Hooke’s law. Which quantity has a value that does not change?

options.B: strain
options.C: stress
options.D: Young modulus

questions.questionText: An object is stretched until it reaches the elastic limit. Which statement must describe the stress on the object when it is at the elastic limit?

options.A: It is the maximum stress for which the object obeys Hooke’s law.
options.B: It is the maximum stress that can be applied to the object before it has elastic deformation.
options.C: It is the maximum stress that can be applied to the object before it has plastic deformation.
options.D: It is the maximum stress the object can withstand before it breaks.

questions.questionText: Which statement about progressive waves is correct?

options.B: They can exist in solids but not liquids.
options.C: They decrease in frequency as their speed increases.
options.D: They transfer energy away from their source.

questions.questionText: A cathode-ray oscilloscope (CRO) is used to determine the frequency of a sound wave. The diagram shows the waveform on the screen. The time-base setting is 5.0msdiv–1. What is the best estimate of the frequency of the sound wave?

The warning signal on an ambulance has a frequency of 600Hz. The speed of sound is 330ms–1. The ambulance is travelling with a constant velocity of 25ms–1 towards an observer. The ambulance passes, and then moves away from the observer with no change in velocity. initial position final position of ambulance of ambulance observer Which overall change in observed frequency takes place between the times at which the ambulance is a long way behind the observer and when it is a long way in front of the observer?

Brief pulses of red, blue and green light are emitted from the Sun at the same time. The pulses travel the same distance to reach Mars. Assume that the pulses travel in a vacuum for the full duration of their journey. In which order would these pulses of light arrive at Mars?

options.A: all arrive at the same time
options.B: blue first, then green, then red
options.C: red first, then blue, then green
options.D: red first, then green, then blue

questions.questionText: Two coherent progressive waves from different sources meet at a point. Which condition must be satisfied for there to be zero resultant amplitude at the point where the waves meet?

options.A: The two waves must be emitted from their sources with the same intensity.
options.B: The two waves must be in phase with each other at the point.
options.C: The two waves must be travelling in opposite directions.
options.D: The two waves must have the same amplitude at the point.

questions.questionText: A corridor is 13.2m long and has closed doors that reflect sound at both ends. The speed of sound in the air in the corridor is 330ms–1. 13.2 m closed door closed door wall position of node What is the lowest frequency of sound that could create a stationary wave in the corridor with a node halfway along it?

Water waves of wavelength  are formed in a ripple tank. The waves are diffracted as they pass through a narrow gap of width d (d is greater than ). Which gap width and which wavelength will cause the largest decrease in the amount of diffraction? gap width wavelength

Two loudspeakers X and Y emit sound waves that are in phase and of wavelength 0.75m. An observer O is able to stand anywhere on a straight line that passes through X and Y, as shown. The observer stands at a point where the sound waves from X and Y meet in phase. O X Y What could be the distances OY and XY? distance OY/m distance XY/m

Light of a single wavelength is incident normally on a diffraction grating. The resulting diffraction pattern is displayed on a screen. Which change makes the first orders of intensity maxima further apart from each other on the screen?

options.A: placing the screen closer to the diffraction grating
options.B: using a diffraction grating with less separation between adjacent slits
options.C: using a diffraction grating with more slits but keeping the same separation between adjacent slits
options.D: using light with a shorter wavelength

questions.questionText: For a current-carrying wire, the current can be calculated using the equation shown. I = Anvq What is the meaning of n?

options.A: the number of charge carriers in the wire
options.B: the number of charge carriers multiplied by the volume of the wire
options.C: the number of charge carriers per unit length of the wire
options.D: the number of charge carriers per unit volume of the wire

questions.questionText: In the circuit shown, lamp P is rated 250V, 50W and lamp Q is rated 250V, 200W. The two lamps are connected in series to a 250V power supply. 250 V P Q Assume that the resistance of each lamp remains constant. Which statement most accurately describes what happens when the switch is closed?

options.A: Lamp P emits four times as much power as lamp Q.
options.B: Lamp P emits twice as much power as lamp Q.
options.C: Lamp Q emits four times as much power as lamp P.
options.D: Lamp Q emits twice as much power as lamp P.
